Cs.bar_b_note: Both sides sink on a murky one-mid-tone brown forest floor with no storm sky, light shafts or lightning, a HUD that covers roughly a third of every frame, flat magenta ground-ring telegraphs (A i06-i10, tell2 a-c) instead of physical effects, and a player creature too small to find; B adds frames i12-i15 where the camera sits inside trunks/foliage and the fight disappears.

Ce.bar_b_note: Clean sky and cyan water help, but huge untextured sand slopes that fill most of the frame, with no fog, grade or shadow form, read as a blockout rather than Palworld-class finish; A's watchtower, hut and blue creature give it a focus that B (hut missing at stand 10, uniform grass carpet at stand 09 approach) lacks.

Bg.bar_b_note: The tidal-flat vista is pleasant, but flat-shaded low-poly green boulders, bare tilted sand planes and no atmospheric depth sink it; A has a hut (stand 11 close) and watchtower (stand 12) as focal points, B has neither and only a slope of grass blades.

Rw.bar_b_note: Warm Meadows grass and distant trees are on-palette, but smeared low-res ground textures, flat lighting and prop-on-a-plane staging fall well short; A's after frames tell distinct stories (banner torn down, cage opened with the captive freed, crates toppled, tent collapsed into smoke, banner dropped) while B's mostly leave the Team Tether banners standing (rows 1, 3, 5) or just delete the cage (row 2).

Wk.bar_b_note: A large naturalistic white-and-blue fur canine well above the 1.80 m ruler sits close to the owner style bar on both sides; A is let down by grey/black material dropouts and black boot-like feet in faint mid/end, B by faint mid reading as standing and faint end as an unreadable hunched lump.

Fx.bar_b_note: A's watchtower and gate (stand 19 close), stilt huts (stand 20 close) and the orange hermit crab give genuine place and creature appeal, but bare dune planes, no fog or grade and B's even grass carpet with the buildings gone (stands 19 and 20 close) keep it below shipping finish.

Un.bar_b_note: The best Tidewake vistas (cyan/navy channels, white-fall rock on the horizon, shelled turtle creature) carry A, whose thatched gazebo (stand 01) and hut (stand 02 close) anchor the place, but the flat-lit, featureless sand mass and banded water still read pre-finish, and B loses both buildings.

Hx.bar_b_note: Trees, an arch gate (stand 17 close) and a blue banner camp give this the most lived-in Tidewake read, but evenly scattered grass blades, flat lighting and the creature cut off at the left edge of stand 18 approach keep it below Palworld finish; B also loses the hut at stand 18 close and carpets stand 17 in grass.

Uh.bar_b_note: An appealing, clearly read elder villager with expressive eyes, warm-green earthy costume and a clean silhouette fits a Palworld-adjacent cast on both near-identical sides; he leans more toy-like and cartoon than the naturalistic key art, and is shown on a black void with no lighting context.

Iw.bar_b_note: The white-fall sea stack is a strong distant landmark and A's huts (stands 21 and 22 close) give a focal settlement, but the low-poly rock, flat navy water bands and barren sand slopes with no fog or warm grade sink it; B's close frames are empty sand with a lone banner.

top_changes.change: Break up the bare Tidewake dune planes: sculpt smaller-scale terrain form, add wet/dry sand and dune-ridge colour variation, shoreline wrack and grouped (not evenly scattered) grass clumps, and add sea haze plus a warm day grade so the sand gets real value range and depth.

Keep and frame a focal building or landmark in every named location's close view (the huts, watchtowers and gazebos visible on the stronger sides), and compose cameras so the landmark sits against the sky instead of filling frames with slope.

Make Stormwood fights readable: pull the combat camera clear of trunks, lift the forest floor value and add the purple storm sky and rim light, shrink the HUD, and replace flat magenta ground rings with physical telegraph effects (lightning, flying stones, dust impacts).
